transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-04-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Claire (Aurora VP Eng), Rafael (Aurora SRE), Lina (Aurora PM)

Summary:
Brief follow-up on April 6th production degradation where requests experienced high tail latency and several customer routes fell back to smaller model shards. Discussed RCA, mitigations deployed, permanent fixes, and next steps including benchmarks and runbook updates.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I know time is tight, we'll keep this tight - follow-up from the Apr 6 incident. quick intro, ethan from SE will walk through logs and then we can go through next steps.
[00:18] Claire (Aurora): Thanks Maya. we want to confirm root cause and the timeline for a fix. customers saw timeouts and a lot of 5xxs for about 22 minutes.
[00:27] Ethan (Redwood): Yeah, first off sorry again. We're tracking this as priority. quick TL;DR - there was an aggressive scale-down from Redwood Dedicated autoscaler which caused several inference nodes to drain and clear KV cache. when the traffic spiked, cache cold-start plus model routing fallback caused token latencies to spike and some requests to hit the smaller fallback model which increased error surface.
[00:46] Rafael (Aurora): just to clarify - the customers were on the dedicated pool in us-west-2 right?
[00:53] Ethan (Redwood): correct, dedicated pool in us-west-2, pool id aurora-ded-3, and the autoscaler had an inconsistent health probe under a specific OS kernel patch; draining proceeded even though node still had in-flight sessions, that triggered a hard KV eviction.
[01:12] Lina (Aurora): there was chatter about a K V cash eviction? can you spell that out, i saw a slack clip but hard to parse.
[01:20] Maya (Redwood): sure, sorry transcription – KV cache (key-value cache) we use for prefix cache and KV cache of the attention states. when nodes drained we lost warm KV cache and retries were routed to fallback models. That's why tail latency spiked.
[01:33] Claire (Aurora): ok makes sense. what about SLO / SLA impact? our customer operations logged 1.8% error spike and several timeouts beyond our 300ms target.
[01:43] Ethan (Redwood): agreed, it's outside your SLO. internally we are proposing a one-time credit and refined SLA wording; Maya will follow up on the exact credit amount.
[01:52] Maya (Redwood): yes i'll draft the compensation proposal. we want to be fair.
[02:00] Ethan (Redwood): going into the RCA specifics - root cause: autoscaler bug + kernel probe mismatch triggered premature node termination. secondary factors: lack of warm-cache replication and missing alerting for sustained cache miss rate.
[02:18] Rafael (Aurora): was there an issue with model compilation or quantization causing the fallback? we saw different logits when fallback happened.
[02:27] Ethan (Redwood): good question. no model corruption; fallback was intentional routing to smaller variant to preserve availability when the main shard capacity dropped. the smaller variant has different tokenization behavior which explains logits discrepancy. not a model integrity issue.
[02:44] Lina (Aurora): what immediate mitigations did you push on Apr 7?
[02:49] Ethan (Redwood): we pushed a hotfix to disable aggressive scale-down, increased the grace period for draining to 10 minutes, and added immediate alerting on sustained KV miss ratio > 15% for 5 minutes. also we rolled back a kernel probe update that was suspected.
[03:05] Claire (Aurora): I saw that but our ops still want stronger guarantees - is pinned instance / reserved option available?
[03:12] Maya (Redwood): yes, Dedicated supports pinned instances and we'll share a recipe. For mission-critical routes we recommend pinned capacity + warm-cache priming. also Redwood Private customers get more control over node lifecycle.
[03:26] Rafael (Aurora): what about automatic warm-cache replications? can you replicate KV to standby nodes?
[03:32] Ethan (Redwood): we have prefix/KV caching but not full active-active replication across all nodes today. we are prototyping async replication to standby nodes; short-term workaround is shortening cache rebuild time by priming and adding scheduled warmers. long-term we'll look at stronger replication.
[03:48] Claire (Aurora): timeline - when do you expect a permanent fix?
[03:52] Ethan (Redwood): patch for autoscaler will land in the next two weeks; target deploy to staging by 2027-04-20 and production by 2027-04-26 after validation. post-deploy we'll run a targeted loadtest.
[04:05] Maya (Redwood): we'll also update runbook and add a step to immediately pin nodes for any route with >10% critical traffic during incidents.
[04:13] Rafael (Aurora): can Redwood run a replay of our April 6 traffic so we can validate? we have the replay bucket ready.
[04:19] Ethan (Redwood): yes please share the replay bucket location and sample traffic profile. we will run a 2-hour warm-cache test and report P50/P95/P99.
[04:28] Lina (Aurora): also want the postmortem doc - we need something we can share internally.
[04:33] Maya (Redwood): we'll send the postmortem draft and include the timeline and remediation steps, and the draft of SLA credit.
[04:40] Claire (Aurora): on monitoring, can you add a dashboard tile for cache miss ratio and model fallback counts? that would help our SREs.
[04:48] Ethan (Redwood): yes, we'll add dashboard widgets and a webhook to your pager when fallback > 5% for 10m.
[04:56] Rafael (Aurora): one more, are there any compliance concerns with us sharing detailed logs? we have PII constraints.
[05:03] Maya (Redwood): we understand. we'll share redacted logs and a CDP access link; for full logs we'll use your KMS integration and S3 bucket access control so nothing leaves your account.
[05:16] Claire (Aurora): ok great. can we also get a quick note on mitigation options cost impact? we need to present to finance.
[05:24] Maya (Redwood): yes we'll include cost delta for pinned capacity vs. autoscaled—rough numbers in the follow-up.
[05:31] Ethan (Redwood): quick note on follow-ups from our side: collect autoscaler logs for the impacted window (nodes 12-14), prepare flamegraphs, run replay with pinning and without and capture tail latency.
[05:46] Lina (Aurora): i'll own the traffic sample and share by EOD Friday.
[05:52] Claire (Aurora): thanks, appreciate the responsiveness.
[06:00] Maya (Redwood): recap and next steps: we'll share postmortem draft, patch ETA, runbook updates, and schedule the loadtest. action items and owners will be in the email follow-up. thanks everyone.
